source_document_title: NPL Report MATC(A)82 -- A Guide to Best Practice for Electronic Materials Dispensing

retrieved_passages.text: For a given needle size dispensing a larger volume will produce a flatter paste deposit. Volume is directly proportional to dispense time; deposit diameter increases with volume, rate of increase reducing with volume; the deposit height remains unchanged i.e. it is defined by the footed needle design.

retrieved_passages.section: 3.5 Missing Dots and Big Dot Small Dot Defect (Solder Paste)
retrieved_passages.text: If the volume of paste dispensed from the needle is too small the paste may not make contact, or properly wet and adhere to the copper PCB pad. This results in a dispensing defect known as a missed dot or big dot/small dot. The hallmark of this problem is a very small or missing dot, followed by a larger over-sized dot at the next deposition point.

For a given needle size dispensing a larger volume of adhesive will produce a taller, thinner adhesive deposit. Volume is directly proportional to dispense time; deposit radius increases with volume, but this rate of increase reduces with increasing volume; the deposit height also increases with volume.

retrieved_passages.section: 4.5 Missing Dots, and, Big Dot Small Dot Defect (SM Adhesive)
retrieved_passages.text: If the volume of adhesive dispensed from the needle is too small it may not make contact, or properly wet and so adhere to the copper PCB pad. This results in a dispensing defect known as a missed dot, or big dot/small dot, as was discussed in section 3.5. The hallmark of this problem is a very small or missing dot, followed by a larger over-sized dot at the next deposition point.

For a given needle size dispensing a larger volume will produce a flatter ICA deposit. Volume is directly proportional to dispense time; deposit radius increases with volume, the rate of increase being greater than for height; the deposit height increases with volume.

retrieved_passages.section: 5.5 Missing Dots and Big Dot Small Dot Defect (ICA)
retrieved_passages.text: This is very similar to the issues encountered previously with solder paste and SM adhesive, as discussed in sections 3.5 and 4.5.

retrieved_passages.section: Visual signature reference (curated, not matc82 itself)
retrieved_passages.text: Row 11 -- Inconsistent size/shape/volume: not a single-dot signature, array-level -- diameters scattered across many positions with no fixed direction (not uniformly big or small). Only visible comparing across the array, not from any one dot. Source: matc82 sections 3.4/4.4/5.4 trend framing.

synthesized_answer: Across all three material classes matc82 covers (solder paste, SM adhesive, ICA), dispensed volume is directly proportional to dispense time, and deposit size grows with volume (secs 3.4/4.4/5.4). When the commanded volume sits near the marginal-wetting boundary, the material intermittently fails to properly wet the pad: that shot reads as a small or missing dot, and the un-deposited material carries over onto the needle tip and adds to the *next* dispense, which then reads oversized (secs 3.5/4.5/5.5, the 'missing dot / big dot-small dot' mechanism). Because this carryover is triggered by a marginal, not-always-true condition, it does not push every dot in one direction -- it produces a scatter of both oversized and undersized dots across the array with no fixed bias, which is exactly the array-level signature distinguishing 'inconsistent size' from a uniform over- or under-dispense.
root_cause_hypothesis: Marginal dispense volume / wetting failure with carryover to the next shot (matc82 secs 3.5, 4.5, 5.5), evidenced at the array level by simultaneous oversized and undersized deposits rather than a one-directional shift.
